descriptors.definition: Taxpayers are permitted to appear through a registered valuer before any income tax authority or the Appellate Tribunal regarding asset valuation matters. This representation right excludes personal attendance mandates required under section 131 for examination on oath or affirmation.
inclusion: Representation before tax authorities for asset valuation
Representation before the Appellate Tribunal for valuation matters
exclusion: Personal attendance ordered under section 131 for examination on oath or affirmation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general authorized representation under section 288 by being specifically restricted to valuation proceedings.

descriptors.definition: Assessees may attend proceedings before income tax authorities or the Appellate Tribunal through a written authorized representative. Eligible representatives include relatives, regular employees, scheduled bank officers, legal practitioners, and qualified chartered accountants meeting specific independence criteria.
inclusion: Written authorization for legal and financial representation
Qualified accountants and legal practitioners acting on behalf of assessees
exclusion: Auditor-disqualified individuals acting as company accountants
nearby_distinctions: Unlike registered valuers who focus solely on valuation, authorized representatives can handle general proceedings under the Act.

descriptors.concept_name: Power To Tender Immunity From Prosecution [Section 291]
descriptors.definition: The Central Government can grant immunity from prosecution and penalties if deemed necessary in the public interest to obtain direct or indirect evidence of income concealment or tax evasion. Non-compliance with conditions or willful concealment allows the government to withdraw the immunity and initiate trial or penalties.
inclusion: Grants of immunity from prosecution and penalties by the Central Government
Withdrawal of immunity upon breach of conditions or false evidence
exclusion: Situations where conditions of immunity are fully met without concealment
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general appeals and dispute resolution mechanisms as it is a discretionary executive power specifically tied to securing cooperative evidence.

descriptors.concept_name: Cognizance Of Offences And Bar Of Suits In Civil Courts [Sections 292 And 293]
descriptors.definition: Offences under the Act can only be tried by a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class. Civil courts are barred from entertaining suits to set aside or modify proceedings or orders, and protection is granted to government officers for actions taken in good faith.
inclusion: Jurisdiction restrictions for criminal trials under the Act
Immunity from civil suits and legal protection for official acts done in good faith
exclusion: Trials by courts inferior to a first-class magistrate
Proceedings or suits where official action lacks good faith
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from tax assessment provisions by establishing judicial boundaries and immunities for enforcement authorities.

descriptors.definition: The probation and admonition provisions under specific criminal procedure and probation laws are rendered inapplicable to individuals convicted of offences under this Act. An exception is carved out for convicted persons who are under eighteen years of age.
instrument_references: Section 360 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
inclusion: Exclusion of general probation laws for tax offence convicts
Age-based exception for offenders under 18 years
exclusion: Non-tax criminal offences governed by general criminal statutes
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general sentencing provisions by explicitly overriding standard criminal probation benefits for tax law violations.

descriptors.concept_name: Return Of Income Etc. Not To Become Invalid [Section 292B]
descriptors.definition: Returns, assessments, notices, and other proceedings are not invalidated merely due to mistakes, defects, or omissions if they substantially conform to the intent and purpose of the Act. This provision prevents technical procedural errors from voiding administrative documents that achieve their intended statutory purpose.
inclusion: Typographical, arithmetical, and minor procedural errors in notices or returns
Documents that align in substance and effect with the statutory intent
exclusion: Defects or mistakes that fundamentally alter the substance or violate the primary intent of the Act
nearby_distinctions: Focused on substantive conformity of written documentation, whereas section 292BB deals specifically with the procedural curing of notice service defects.

descriptors.concept_name: Notice Deemed To Be Valid In Certain Circumstances [Section 292Bb]
descriptors.definition: An assessee who participates in assessment or reassessment proceedings is precluded from later challenging the validity, timeliness, or manner of notice service. This deeming provision does not apply if the assessee raises a specific objection regarding service defects prior to the completion of the assessment or reassessment.
inclusion: Curing of defective, delayed, or unserved notices through assessee participation
Waiver of service objections upon cooperation in proceedings
exclusion: Cases where the assessee formally objects to service defects before assessment completion
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from document-level errors under section 292B by specifically addressing personal notice service and recipient participation waivers.

descriptors.concept_name: Presumption As To Assets, Books Of Account, Etc. [Section 292C]
descriptors.definition: Books of account, documents, money, and assets found during searches, surveys, or requisition proceedings are legally presumed to belong to the person in possession. Further presumptions apply that document contents are true, signatures and handwriting belong to the purported authors, and executed documents were duly stamped and executed.
inclusion: Evidentiary presumptions regarding ownership of seized assets and documents
Assumptions of truth and correct execution for books of account and records
exclusion: Materials and assets not found in the possession or control of the person during search, survey, or requisition
nearby_distinctions: Extends the evidentiary presumptions originally created for search operations to regular assessments and survey proceedings.

descriptors.concept_name: Authority Empowered To Grant An Approval Under The Income Tax Act, 1961 Deemed To Have Power To Withdraw The Approval Granted [Section 293C]
descriptors.definition: Statutory authorities that grant approvals for tax incentive benefits inherently possess the authority to withdraw such approvals at any time. Any withdrawal requires recording written reasons and providing the concerned assessee with a reasonable opportunity to show cause.
inclusion: Revocation of prior tax incentive approvals by the granting authority
Mandatory issuance of a show-cause notice and recording of reasons prior to withdrawal
exclusion: Withdrawal of approvals without granting an opportunity of being heard
nearby_distinctions: Differs from regular assessment powers by targeting specific incentive approvals and establishing a uniform revocation mechanism.

descriptors.concept_name: Act To Have Effect Pending Legislative Provision For Charge Of Tax [Section 294]
descriptors.definition: If a Central Act fails to enact income tax charging provisions by April 1st of an assessment year, the existing tax act remains operational. It continues to function using either the preceding year provisions or the current parliamentary bill proposals, whichever proves more favourable to the assessee.
inclusion: Continuation of tax collection mechanisms during legislative delays
Application of the more beneficial tax rate between prior laws and pending bills
exclusion: Scenarios where regular charging provisions are enacted on or before April 1st
nearby_distinctions: Acts as a temporary transitional safeguard specifically for tax charging continuity rather than general administrative rule-making.

descriptors.definition: The Central Board of Direct Taxes is empowered to formulate subordinate rules under central government control to implement the Act, which must be placed before Parliament. These rules carry statutory force equivalent to enactment sections provided they remain consistent with, supplementary to, and non-derogatory of the primary statute.
inclusion: Rule-making authority of the Board
Statutory force and parliamentary oversight of formulated rules
exclusion: Rules that conflict with, restrict, or adversely affect the operative effect of parent act sections
nearby_distinctions: Differs from primary legislative acts by being subordinate executive regulations that must strictly conform to the parent statute's mandate.

descriptors.concept_name: Schedules To The Income Tax Act, 1961
descriptors.definition: The fourteen schedules appended to the primary legislation provide specialized operational frameworks for specific tax computations and administrative procedures. Notable schedules govern insurance business profit computations, tax recovery procedures, distraint actions, and recognized provident or superannuation funds.
inclusion: Specialized computational rules for insurance profits
Procedures for tax recovery, distraint, and approved retirement funds
exclusion: Core charging sections and general administrative provisions located in the main body of the Act
nearby_distinctions: Serves as statutory appendices that detail procedural and computational mechanisms supplementing core sections.
